title: Building Bridges to the Future of Vocational Psychology: Introduction to the Special Issue
abstract: This special issue reflects a collective effort to re-examine vocational psychology amid major shifts in the modern landscape of work and careers. Since the 2001 Journal of Vocational Behavior special issue on the field’s future, edited by Mark Savickas, economic restructuring, technological acceleration, and widening socioeconomic inequalities have reshaped how people experience work across the lifespan. The 2025 Society for Vocational Psychology conference in Lausanne, Switzerland, adopted “bridges” as its theme to highlight needed connections across conceptual, disciplinary, methodological, geographical, and intergenerational divides, while bridging the field’s science and practice. Building on the bridges theme, the eight focal articles in this issue highlight opportunities for disciplinary renewal. These contributions span theoretical frameworks, sociopolitical realities, research methodologies, social justice views, technological advancements, assessment and intervention approaches, and professional identity. This introduction outlines the rationale for the special issue, establishes the bridge metaphor as an organizing frame, and previews the eight articles. Our closing article reflects on the varied perspectives offered by the eight articles to outline next steps for reenergizing and advancing the field.
